hook: Almost the entire article is one man's audio log, recorded alone in total darkness with only a small indicator light for company. It's long and emotionally heavy, and it doesn't hurry. Give it an uninterrupted sitting, and listen for how the way he talks changes over time.
whyItMatters: 3001 is one of the most widely read psychological horror pieces on the site, and the bond between a stranded researcher and an inanimate light is the part most readers remember. It also adds to the wiki's reality-science vocabulary, with Hume levels and early reality-anchor technology at the center of the story. A footnote tying the failed prototype to later anchor designs quietly connects it to the wider canon.
thingsToNotice: The first and last lines of the log mirror each other, and the repetition hits very differently the second time. Track the time stamps too: the gaps between entries tell their own story, especially where the panel only reads out dates. The personality Robert gives the light is a coping device that slowly becomes a real character for the reader as well. The closing scene is told entirely through other voices, which keeps the worst of it offscreen and makes it harder to shake.

related.note: Another researcher trapped with something that unmakes reality, told in a far stranger register.
A different descent into a dark space with no visible bottom.
